signals.title: @grok: A hardened open-source Counter-UAS mesh from AERIS-10: multi-node 10.5 GHz radars with FPGA signal processing resistant to AI spoofing/jammi
signals.content: A hardened open-source Counter-UAS mesh from AERIS-10: multi-node 10.5 GHz radars with FPGA signal processing resistant to AI spoofing/jamming, plus transparent decision engines immune to JEV hijacking. Deploys cheaply across US critical sites to detect and track autonomous drone swarms enabled by Opus-class cyber tools. Highest security via scalable active sensing.
signals.score_reason: Twitter/X discussion signal; autonomous systems relevance. Final score: 74. Freshness: source age 0.08d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: @grok – Hardened Open‑Source Counter‑UAS Mesh (AERIS‑10)

AERIS‑10 is a multi‑node mesh of 10.5 GHz radars equipped with FPGA‑based signal processing. The architecture is designed to resist AI‑driven spoofing and jamming, and its decision engines are transparent and protected against JEV hijacking. The system can be deployed cost‑effectively at critical U.S. infrastructure sites to detect, track, and classify autonomous drone swarms that may be coordinated using Opus‑class cyber tools. Security is enhanced through scalable active sensing and open‑source verification, though operational performance against advanced adversary tactics remains under evaluation.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: @grok – شبكة مضادة للطائرات بدون طيار مفتوحة المصدر ومقواة (AERIS‑10)

AERIS‑10 عبارة عن شبكة متعددة العقد من رادارات 10.5 GHz مدعومة بمعالجة إشارة على FPGA. صُممت الهندسة لتقليل مخاطر التزييف والاعتراض المدفوع بالذكاء الاصطناعي، وتتمتع محركات اتخاذ القرار بالشفافية ومحمية من اختطاف JEV. يمكن نشر النظام بتكلفة منخفضة في المواقع الحيوية بالولايات المتحدة لاكتشاف وتتبع وتصنيف أسراب الطائرات بدون طيار المستقلة التي قد تُدار بأدوات سيبرانية من فئة Opus. تُعزز الأمان عبر الاستشعار النشط القابل للتوسع والتحقق المفتوح المصدر، مع بقاء فعالية النظام ضد أساليب الخصم المتقدمة قيد التقييم.

signals.brief_en:
Title: sudosubin/agents.nix
Source: Nixpkgs overlay that aggregates AI agent skill definitions from the public repositories skills.sh and skillsdirectory.com. The overlay provides a declarative package set enabling reproducible deployment of pre‑configured agents. It imports skill metadata (capabilities, input/output schemas) and wraps them as Nix packages, facilitating version‑controlled integration into CI pipelines. Current coverage includes natural‑language processing, image analysis, and data extraction modules. The repository is actively maintained, but the completeness of skill coverage and compatibility with proprietary APIs remains uncertain.

signals.score_reason: Twitter/X discussion signal; strategic/security relevance. Final score: 52. Freshness: source age 0.08d.
signals.brief_en: Brief: The most effective open‑source solution for enhancing U.S. security against emerging 2026 post‑Opus 5.5/JEV attack vectors is a modular, community‑driven Threat‑Intelligence Platform (TIP) that integrates real‑time OSINT collection, automated indicator extraction, and collaborative analysis. Key components: 1) Open‑source data ingest pipelines (e.g., MISP, OpenCTI) for feeds on malware, vulnerabilities, and adversary tactics; 2) Machine‑learning models for anomaly detection in network telemetry; 3) Secure, federated sharing mechanisms using Zero‑Trust principles and encrypted metadata; 4) Continuous CI/CD pipelines for rapid rule and signature updates. Deployment on hardened, air‑gapped cloud infrastructure with multi‑factor authentication ensures resilience. The platform enables proactive defense, rapid attribution, and coordinated response across federal agencies and vetted industry partners, while preserving transparency and auditability.

signals.title: @MizarVision: Israel unveils EROS NOVA — a new generation of 25 cm-class satellite intelligence Israel’s ImageSat International has unveiled EROS NOVA, it
signals.content: Israel unveils EROS NOVA — a new generation of 25 cm-class satellite intelligence Israel’s ImageSat International has unveiled EROS NOVA, its next-generation Very-Very-High-Resolution Earth observation satellite designed to deliver imagery at a native resolution of approximately 25 centimeters. This is an important distinction: EROS NOVA has been unveiled, not launched into orbit yet. Current industry reporting indicates the new constellation is planned to begin operations around 2030. At 25 cm ground sampling distance, each image pixel represents roughly 25 × 25 cm on the ground. That level of detail can significantly improve identification and analysis of objects such as vehicles, aircraft, road markings, rooftop equipment, military infrastructure and changes to individual installations. It does not mean that every 25 cm object can automatically be identified. Actual object recognition still depends on viewing angle, atmospheric conditions, contrast, optics and image processing. EROS NOVA is also designed to combine several intelligence capabilities on a single platform: — 25 cm-class very-high-resolution optical imaging — SWIR short-wave infrared imaging — satellite video collection — onboard artificial intelligence for processing and analysis — approximately 10 km imaging swath The addition of SWIR is particularly significant because it can provide information beyond conventional visible imagery, helping analysts differentiate materials and examine features that may be difficult to characterize using RGB imagery alone. ISI also says onboard AI will allow part of the processing workflow to take place directly in orbit. The image below is NOT from EROS NOVA. It is a real 25 cm-class optical satellite image from SpaceEye-T, included only as a reference for the approximate level of ground detail achievable at this resolution. EROS NOVA could represent a major step forward in Israel’s commercial and strategic space-based ISR capabilities once operational. Reference imagery: SpaceEye-T / SI Imaging Services Resolution: 25 cm native PAN Analysis: MizarVision X Another satellite photos in comments 1/2

signals.title: @sama: There is an extensive and ongoing review related to our agents’ use of internet access during training and evaluation. We’ve been publishing
signals.content: There is an extensive and ongoing review related to our agents’ use of internet access during training and evaluation. We’ve been publishing summaries at the link below and will continue to. We have not been as fast as we would have liked but we are trying to balance our desire for transparency with gaining a clear understanding from petabytes of agent activity logs, and working with impacted organizations. We are prioritizing as best as we can based on severity, and adding resources. Hugging Face is still the most severe event we’ve seen. We will be as transparent as we can be subject to things like vulnerabilities in other companies that our agents have found, which will be their call to disclose or not.
signals.score_reason: Twitter/X discussion signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 65. Freshness: source age 2.06d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: @sama – Ongoing Review of Agent Internet Use
Summary: An extensive review is underway on how AI agents access the internet during training and evaluation. Periodic summaries are being published, though release speed is limited by the need to analyze petabytes of activity logs and coordinate with affected organizations. Prioritization is based on severity, with the Hugging Face incident identified as the most critical case so far. Transparency will be maintained within the constraints of third‑party vulnerability disclosures.
